title: Rabbi Chiyya of Kefar Techumin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: At the end of [Jerusalem Talmud Terumot](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.11.5.11) and in [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.2.1.20), Rabbi Abbahu reports what Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhmai taught him. Rabbi Zeira said to him: “And what was his merit?” He said to him: “He was a great man and expert in our Mishnah; Rabbi Chiyya of Kefar Techumin presented him before Rabbi (identified by Hyman as the second Rabbi Yehudah Nesia), and Rabbi appointed him a sage.”[^2]

In [Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1, folio 3b](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.1.1.35), he disagrees with Rabbi Berekhyah; one said: “Even the whole world is not worth one word of the Torah,” etc.

notes.text: Saved Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:1 explains פירשה as Rabbi Chiyya publicizing Yonatan ben Akhmai’s merits before Rabbi, who appointed Yonatan a sage. It is not merely explaining a ruling followed by an anonymous “they appointed.” The Nasi II identification remains Hyman’s gloss. Saved Guggenheimer Peah 1:1 explicitly has דבר אחד, supporting “one word” for ד״א, with חד אמר for ח״א.

The Hebrew in [Terumot 11:5:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.11.5.11) reads “before Rav,” while [Shabbat 2:1:20](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.2.1.20) reads “before Rabbi,” as Hyman quotes it. [Seder HaDorot 1277](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1277&lang=en) records both forms as well as Rabbi Chiyya’s exchange with Rabbi Berekhyah in Peah.
